characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy focuses on proving that platform‑neutral and fallback authentication mechanisms can be securely implemented within Denmark’s digital identity ecosystem. It guides the design, development, and testing of demonstrators—such as FIDO2/WebAuthn on GrapheneOS and browser‑based or hardware‑token fallbacks—while balancing scope, cost, and risk. Success metrics include demonstrator completion, documented security assessments, and evidence of compliance with eIDAS/NSIS standards. The strategy’s outputs provide the hard technical evidence that underpins policy proposals, procurement language, and EU‑level advocacy, thereby translating engineering feasibility into actionable policy leverage.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: By delivering concrete, secure demonstrators, the Technical Feasibility Strategy amplifies the Policy Advocacy Strategy’s arguments for platform neutrality and directly informs the Procurement Influence Strategy’s language requirements. The evidence also supports the EU Standards Engagement Strategy by showcasing compliance with eIDAS/NSIS, creating a virtuous cycle of technical proof and policy momentum.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A narrow focus on technical demonstrators can delay policy engagement, constraining the Policy Advocacy Strategy’s ability to act swiftly. Over‑emphasis on specific platforms may also limit the Procurement Influence Strategy’s flexibility, as vendors may perceive the requirements as too prescriptive, potentially stalling procurement negotiations.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the legislative and procurement environment to reduce Denmark’s reliance on foreign platform vendors. It frames platform neutrality as a resilience and sovereignty imperative, leveraging continuity‑of‑service and supplier‑concentration risks to persuade Digitaliseringsstyrelsen and the Folketinget’s digital policy committee. Success metrics include formal policy proposals adopted, procurement documents amended, and stakeholder support quantified. The strategy balances continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability to broaden coalition appeal while guarding against regulatory capture by incumbent vendors and ensuring alignment with EU digital identity frameworks.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: The Policy Advocacy Strategy synergizes with the Coalition Building Strategy by mobilizing a broad stakeholder base, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy by translating policy goals into concrete procurement language. Together, they create a unified front that amplifies Denmark’s platform‑neutral agenda across legislative, procurement, and market arenas.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing heavily on policy can delay technical progress, constraining the Technical Feasibility Strategy’s ability to produce demonstrators on schedule. Aggressive procurement language may also alienate potential vendors, limiting the Procurement Influence Strategy’s flexibility and potentially stalling procurement negotiations. Additionally, an overly broad coalition may dilute focus, creating friction with the Coalition Building Strategy.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy assembles a diverse network of civil‑society groups, privacy advocates, academics, security experts, and internal stakeholders to amplify the platform‑neutral agenda. By coordinating joint statements, public campaigns, and stakeholder meetings, the strategy increases political pressure on Digitaliseringsstyrelsen and the Folketinget. Success metrics include coalition size, stakeholder engagement frequency, and measurable influence on policy discussions. The strategy also manages internal alignment to mitigate conflicting priorities and maintain a unified advocacy narrative. Furthermore, the coalition serves as a conduit for rapid feedback on technical developments, ensuring that policy proposals remain grounded in realistic feasibility.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: The Coalition Building Strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing a broad base of support, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy by creating a unified stakeholder voice that strengthens procurement language. Together, they amplify Denmark’s platform‑neutral agenda across political, procurement, and technical domains.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Expanding the coalition too rapidly can dilute focus, creating friction with the Technical Feasibility Strategy’s tight scope and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy’s need for clear technical positions. A broad coalition may also slow decision‑making, constraining the Procurement Influence Strategy’s ability to negotiate timely procurement language.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy targets the formal procurement process for AltID and related digital identity services to embed platform‑neutral and fallback requirements. It drafts precise language, scoring criteria, and compliance checks that compel vendors to demonstrate reduced reliance on Apple or Google infrastructure. Success metrics include the inclusion of platform‑neutral clauses in procurement documents, the number of vendors meeting fallback criteria, and measurable reductions in supplier concentration risk. The strategy also monitors vendor responses to mitigate gaming and ensures that procurement remains transparent and aligned with Denmark’s digital sovereignty objectives.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy by embedding policy goals into formal procurement language, and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy by aligning procurement criteria with emerging EU digital identity standards. Together, they create a coherent pathway from policy intent to market implementation, reinforcing Denmark’s platform‑neutral agenda across all procurement stages.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Strict procurement requirements can constrain the Technical Feasibility Strategy’s design flexibility, forcing vendors to adopt specific platforms. Over‑rigid language may also alienate potential coalition partners, limiting the Coalition Building Strategy’s influence. Balancing prescriptive language with technical openness is essential to avoid stalling procurement negotiations.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy positions Denmark as a proactive contributor to the European Digital Identity Wallet framework, advocating for platform‑neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms. It monitors EU technical working groups, submits position papers, and participates in standard‑setting workshops. Success metrics include the adoption of platform‑neutral clauses in EU standards, the number of EU submissions accepted, and measurable influence on the European Digital Identity Wallet roadmap. The strategy also ensures that Denmark’s national requirements align with EU interoperability and resilience goals, creating a feedback loop between national policy and European standards development.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy synergizes with the Procurement Influence Strategy by ensuring that procurement criteria reflect emerging EU standards, and with the Policy Advocacy Strategy by aligning national policy goals with EU interoperability objectives. This alignment accelerates the adoption of platform‑neutral requirements across both national and European digital identity ecosystems.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU standards may lag behind national technical innovations, creating a conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy’s rapid demonstrator development. A broad EU engagement focus can also dilute the Coalition Building Strategy’s national messaging, constraining its ability to maintain a unified stance on platform neutrality.
